name: District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority (DC Water)
outfalls_source: https://services2.arcgis.com/kZWfT06uhil5hMQO/arcgis/rest/services/CSOSheds_InteractiveMap_CSOOutfalls/FeatureServer/0 (46 points, labels and photos, 2017) and the EPA ECHO national CSO inventory (56 rows for DC0021199 incl. separated outfalls and tunnel overflows 003A and 019A)
notification_channel: News releases and public notices at https://www.dcwater.com/about-dc-water/media/news (no RSS; email via the Everbridge sign-up https://www.dcwater.com/customer-center/alerts-and-notifications/dc-water-alert-notification-signups); CSO Event Indicator Lights (one on the Potomac near the mouth of Rock Creek, four on the Anacostia; red during a CSO, yellow for 24 hours after); signs at each CSO outfall; quarterly CSO reports (PDF); 24-hour Command Center 202-612-3400; X @dcwater, Facebook DCWaterSewerAuth, Instagram dc.water
notes: Only CSO/SSO permittee in DC. EPA Region 3 issues the permit (DC is not NPDES-authorized), so DC Water files SSO/CSO noncompliance reports in EPA eReporting: 140 current SOBE rows 2023-03 to 2026-09. Permit effective 2018-08-26, expired August 2023, administratively continued. Website says 48 potentially active CSO outfalls; the Q2 2026 model table lists 42 active (Anacostia 11, Potomac 8, Rock Creek 23), outfalls 015-018 'consolidated to tunnel system', 006/025/026/031/037/053/057/058 separated. Anacostia River Tunnel System (incl. Northeast Boundary Tunnel, in service 2023) controls the Anacostia; Potomac River Tunnel under construction (TBMs Mary and Emily, 2025-2026); Piney Branch tunnel ground broken 2026. Also owns the Potomac Interceptor (~50 miles from Dulles through Virginia and Maryland to the Potomac Pumping Station), which collapsed on 2026-01-19 at Clara Barton Parkway, Montgomery County MD (~243 million gallons): its overflows are reported under DC0021199 although they happen in Maryland. Collection system population 689,545 (ECHO collection_system_permit), percent CSS field 56. CSO Q3 2026: 154.61 MG total (Potomac 137.83, Rock Creek 11.24, Anacostia 5.54 at CSO 010 O Street pumped overflow). ECHO DFR: https://echo.epa.gov/detailed-facility-report?fid=110029030144.

name: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC Water) — Anacostia Wastewater Pumping Station (cross-border; Maryland agent owns)
notification_channel: WSSC Water news releases (joint notices with DC Water, e.g. 2025-07-27 'Proactive Notification of Possible Controlled Emergency Sewage Overflow into Beaverdam Creek and Anacostia River'; signs 'urging residents to avoid these waterways for up to 30 days')
notes: Listed only so the DC Anacostia pages can name the upstream operator whose pumping station (1700 Andalusia Lane, Capitol Heights) sends 60-65 MGD into DC Water's 108-inch Anacostia Force Main and can overflow to Beaverdam Creek at the DC line. Maryland/WSSC have no rows in EPA SOBE. Permit number not looked up (Maryland agent).
